lines.text: This thirty dollar fake Makita claims almost twice the torque of the real one.
And the real one costs 138 dollars so on paper you'd be crazy to pay five times more.
beats: ai:two piles of dollar bills on a workbench one five times bigger than the other

lines.text: They even weigh the same down to one single gram.
But on the torque rig the fake makes just 91 foot pounds.
That's less than a quarter of what its listing promised so those specs are basically fan fiction.
beats: ai:an open glowing fantasy storybook with magic sparkles on a dark workbench

lines.text: And the real Makita hits 178 out of its promised 210.
Because inside an impact wrench a spinning hammer slams the anvil thousands of times a minute.
beats: ai:cutaway of a steel hammer slamming a steel anvil inside a power tool with sparks

lines.text: And the Makita's hammer is 44 grams heavier and spins faster so every hit carries more energy.
beats: ai:slow motion steel hammer striking metal with a glowing shockwave

lines.text: So it pulls lug nuts in 35 seconds instead of 49 which is almost a third faster.
Then he drops both again and again until the fake's handle snaps.
But thirty bucks for a brushless motor is still a crazy good deal.
So would you pay five times more for the real one?
